newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-DYNAMO TAKE LEAGUE LEAD FROM ROTOR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DYNAMO TAKE LEAGUE LEAD FROM ROTOR.

text.p: Dynamo Moscow took advantage of leaders Rotor Volgograd's stumble, beating Zhemchuzhina Sochi 1-0 at home on Saturday to go top of the Russian league.
Andrei Kobelev scored the winner in the 64th minute, giving the Muscovites 25 points after 12 matches, while Rotor remained with 24 after a tough 3-2 loss to Alania in Vladikavkaz.
Last year's runners-up Vladikavkaz, powered by Igor Yanovsky's two first-half goals, were able to beat Rotor before a highly partisan home crowd of 40,000.
Defending champions Spartak Moscow kept pace with Dynamo's 25 points with a 3-1 win over city rivals Lokomotiv.

For Spartak, the score was just reward for constant pressure. Dmitry Alenichev's superb through ball carved open Lokomotiv's well-organised defence to allow Igor Titov to open the scoring in the 69th minute.

Before that Spartak's Alexander Filimonov saved a penalty from Alexei Kosolapov in the 21st and did well to stop Vitaly Veselov, who got clean through in the 66th. Only the underside of the crossbar kept out a long-range Yevgeny Kharlachev effort that had Filimonov well beaten just before half time.
Lokomotiv, who claimed an 85th-minute consolation goal from Alexander Borodyuk, should not go into their next game -- the Cup final against Dynamo Moscow on June 11 -- too downhearted.
Russia coach Boris Ignatyev will be pleased to see Andrei Tikhonov, in his first full game after months out injured, notch Spartak's second and third in the space of six minutes.

But facing a lively Israeli side in next week's vital World Cup qualifier, he will be less happy with the way key links in the Russian defence, Spartak's Ramiz Mamedov and Dmitry Klestov, seemed happier going forward while leaving spaces at the back.
